text: A script that runs once by hand isn't enough for a real source. This lesson makes Lesson 17's script run unattended, reliably, with a real record of what happened each time.

Real logging replaces bare print statements. basicConfig writes every run's outcome to a log file with a timestamp and severity level — info for a normal run, error for a failure, caught and re-raised so a scheduler can detect it.
Scheduling this script means it runs on a fixed cadence with no human remembering to trigger it. Windows Task Scheduler runs it daily, set to run whether a user is logged on or not.
The equivalent on Linux or macOS is a one-line crontab entry, running the same script every night at 3 AM with no one in the loop.

This directly closes one of Lesson 1's five real gaps: a new raw source loaded by hand, when someone remembers, replaced by an automatic, logged, scheduled process. Next: protecting everything built so far with a real CI/CD gate.
